prompt: A crisp black-and-white textbook lithograph of a single 5x8 recipe card on a white enamel prep table, seen straight from above. The card’s layout is the bold choice: four small glass jars drawn at the corners of a diamond, from separated oil and acid at left to one finished emulsified vinaigrette jar at right, with thin black arrows tracing two alternate legal paths around the diamond. Along each edge, small pencil tally marks and tiny serif numbers mark local cost; the upper path’s sum visibly differs from the lower path’s sum. Keep the square’s center mostly empty except for a faint graphite smudge, as if the discrepancy is trapped inside the loop. Minimal grayscale palette, thin outlines, serif labels, flat even overhead light, clean symmetrical composition, white background, slight oil ring and worn card edges, visual language borrowed from mathematical line diagrams rather than photography.
caption: Cookculus pins order effects to local loop defects: two pencil-marked routes around a vinaigrette diamond reach the same jar with different tally sums.

A green and dark blue book cover fills the image, with the title “Lectures on Colonialism and Publics” set in small yellow text near the upper left and the author name “Mahmood Kooria” below it in white. The composition is divided into horizontal color blocks, with a bright green band across the top and a large deep blue field below, plus small publisher marks and text along the lower left edge.

A small black-background coordinate diagram shows white x- and y-axes crossing at the origin, with labels “x,” “y,” “0,” and a marked point near the top labeled “(1, 2).” Two narrow white line segments form a slim wedge from the origin to that point, with arrowheads along the segments, and the letter “C” appears beside the shape; the image is rendered as simple white line art with a stark monochrome palette.
